title: DAYLIGHT SAVINGS TIME
full_story:
Whether digital or analog, Illinoisans will set their clocks forward Saturday night as daylight saving time returns.

Despite years of debate in Congress about ending the twice-yearly clock change, daylight saving time remains in place for 2026.  That means most of the US, will “spring forward” on March 8th.

Most smartphones, computers and other connected devices will update automatically.  But people will need to manually change non-smart devices such as microwaves, older car radios and analog wall clocks.

Efforts to eliminate the biannual clock change have stalled at both the federal and state levels.

In 2022, the US Senate unanimously passed the Sunshine Protection Act, which would have made daylight saving time permanent.  The House did not take it up.  The bill resurfaced in Congress in 2025 but again failed to advance.

President Donald Trump has voiced support for ending the clock changes.  In December 2024, then-president-elect Trump said he wanted to eliminate daylight saving time and move to year-round standard time.  He reiterated that stance in April 2025.

Until Congress passes legislation and a president signs it into law, the clock changes will continue nationwide.

Clocks will move back one hour, giving most Americans an extra hour of sleep on November 1st.

title: GET OUT THE VOTE TOUR
full_story:
Illinois gubernatorial candidate and former State Senator Darren Bailey along with his running mate Aaron Del Mar are launching a statewide 7-day “Get Out The Vote” bus tour.

The Bus Tour will start Monday at 9am at Countryside Campers in Pana.  The tour will make a stop in Flora next Friday, when the candidates stop at the Flora Diner from 6 to 7 pm.  Earlier Friday they will appear in Mt. Carmel at Rosati’s Pizza at 3 pm and at McLeansboro at the Greg James Memorial Park at Noon.

title: CARLYLE POLICE CHIEF CHARGED
full_story:
The former police chief of the Carlyle Police Department is facing several federal charges for allegedly embezzling more than $100,000 for his personal benefit.

A federal grand jury returned a four-count indictment charging Mark A. Pingsterhaus, 52, of Carlyle, with two counts of wire fraud and two counts of theft of government funds.

According to the indictment, Pingsterhaus is facing charges for allegedly embezzling funds from at least January 2017 to November 2025 as police chief for the City of Carlyle and as the chief financial officer for the Carlyle Fire Protection District.

Pingsterhaus is accused of using City of Carlyle and Carlyle Fire Protection District funds for unauthorized and personal expenses like travel, entertainment, goods and services.  In two examples, the indictment states he used the City of Carlyle’s bank card to purchase WNBA tickets and the Caryle Fire Protection District’s bank card to purchase jewelry from Zales.

He is also accused of using funds from the Carlyle Police Department’s Drug and Education Fund for personal expenses.

An indictment is merely an allegation. A defendant is presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

Convictions for wire fraud are punishable by up to 20 years’ imprisonment and theft of government funds can earn up to 10 years in federal prison.

The FBI Springfield Field Office is leading the investigation, and Assistant US Attorney Peter T. Reed is prosecuting the case.

title: IECC SPIN NIGHTS
full_story:
Illinois Eastern Community Colleges (IECC) is hosting a series of Student/Parent Information Nights, known as SPIN Nights, to help prospective students and their families take the next step toward college enrollment.

Each campus will host its own SPIN Night from 5:30 to 7 pm on the following dates, at Olney Central College Spin Night will be held tonight, and at Wabash Valley College on Tuesday, March 17th and at Lincoln Trail College on Thursday, March 19th.  Frontier Community College held there SPIN Night earlier this week.

SPIN Night is designed as a one-stop opportunity for students and parents to explore IECC programs, connect with key staff members, and learn more about the enrollment process.

During the event, attendees can explore academic programs, speak with Financial Aid representatives, schedule advising appointments, learn about student clubs and organizations, and discover support services available through each campus’s Learning Commons.

“SPIN Night is about making college planning simple and approachable for both students and their families,” said Carrie Halbert, IECC Director of Student Engagement and Recruitment.  “We want them to walk in with questions and leave feeling confident about their next steps.”

Halbert said the event allows families to gather information in one setting rather than trying to piece together details on their own.

“Students can meet advisors, talk through financial aid options, and see the support systems we have in place,” Halbert said.  “It’s an opportunity to see firsthand how IECC helps students succeed from day one.”

Registration is encouraged.  Students and parents can scan the QR code included on promotional materials to select the campus and date they plan to attend.

In addition to SPIN Night activities, Lincoln Trail College will also host an Ag Exploration Night on March 19th, giving attendees the opportunity to learn more about agricultural programs and careers.

For more information about SPIN Nights and to register, visit iecc.edu/spin or scan the QR code on event materials.

title: PLUMMER NAMED CAUCUS CHAIR
full_story:
State Senator Jason Plummer was recently named Caucus Chair for the Illinois Senate Republican Caucus.

“I’m grateful for the opportunity to serve as Caucus Chair and to continue working with my colleagues on behalf of the people of Illinois,” said Senator Plummer.  “Our state needs leadership that puts families, taxpayers, and job creators first. That means fighting for lower taxes, more economic opportunity, reliable energy, safer communities, and government transparency.  I’m proud to work alongside Leader Curran as we push back against failed policies and continue advancing a commonsense Republican vision for Illinois.”

Plummer previously served as Assistant Republican Leader and has been a leading voice for Southern Illinois families, workers, farmers, and job creators.  He represents the 55th State Senate District, which encompasses all or portions of Clay, Clinton, Effingham, Fayette, Madison, Marion, Montgomery, Richland, St. Clair, Bond, and Washington Counties.

Senate Minority Leader John Curran said Plummer’s experience and leadership make him well-suited for the role.

“Senator Plummer has proven himself to be a thoughtful and effective leader for our caucus and for the people of Illinois,” said Senate Minority Leader John Curran.  “His service as Assistant Republican Leader demonstrated his ability to bring members together, communicate our message, and advocate for the people of Illinois.  I am proud to continue working alongside Senator Plummer.”

Plummer was first elected to the Illinois Senate in 2018 and has served in caucus leadership since 2021.  As Caucus Chair, he will help guide caucus messaging, legislative priorities, and member coordination for the Illinois Senate Republican caucus.

title: IEMA SEVERE WEATHER PREPAREDNESS
full_story:
The Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland Security (IEMA OHS) is giving tips on how to prepare for severe weather ahead of the spring season.

Thunderstorms, tornadoes, lightning, floods, and power outages are all possibilities that could affect Illinois residents during the Spring season.  March is known as Severe Weather Preparedness Month across many states.

“Millions of dollars in storm damages within the last year shows just how quickly severe weather can impact our communities,” said IEMA OHS Acting Director Theodore Berger.  “We understand that severe weather can be overwhelming, but you don’t have to face it unprepared.  Taking time now to plan and gather essentials can help protect the people and places you care about most.”

Among the tips is to keep all important records and documents in a secure, waterproof container, make an inventory of possessions using lists and photos/videos, insure your property and personal items, know how to shut off your home utilities like electricity, gas, and water, and assemble an emergency kit and “go bag” to help your family for at least three days during extended power outages or in case of evacuation.  If power is out, make sure flashlights with fresh batteries are ready, have a backup cell phone charger fully charged, and remember generators should only be run outside.

For more tips, as well as ideas for a preparedness kit, can be found at https://ready.illinois.gov/plan/emergencykit.html.

title: WALMART TO PAY
full_story:
Walmart will pay $100 million to settle allegations it deceived customers and drivers in its Spark delivery program.

Illinois drivers will receive more than $1.1 million as part of the settlement announced by Attorney General Kwame Raoul.

The settlement resolves claims that Walmart misrepresented pre-tip amounts, base pay and incentive pay to drivers through the Spark app, which the company has used since 2018.

Nearly 1 million drivers have made more than 270 million deliveries nationwide through Spark.

Walmart allegedly made offers to drivers through the app, then split or changed parts of the order after a driver accepted, which resulted in drivers receiving less than the base pay or full tip shown.

The company also allegedly failed to disclose full incentive pay requirements to drivers who only became aware of additional requirements when they were not paid.

Under the settlement, Walmart will pay up to $79 million in restitution.  The company has already paid approximately $63 million directly to drivers, including $1.1 million to Illinois drivers.

Walmart is also paying a total of $11 million to the states, including approximately $1.1 million to Illinois, and an additional $10 million to the Federal Trade Commission.

The company will have to operate an earnings verification program and submit an annual report to the FTC for the next 10 years.

Walmart is also prohibited from modifying orders after drivers accept them or misrepresenting how much a driver will earn.
